text: Variable Eddington factors and tensors: closing moments with angular transport VEF obtains an Eddington closure from angular transport and iterates it with a separate moment system. It uses a scalar factor f in one dimension and a tensor D in multiple dimensions. VET denotes this tensor form, rather than an unrelated physical model. Distinguishing grey models, diffusion and M1 The grey approximation integrates over frequency. VEF/VET instead obtains the pressure closure from an angular distribution. Being grey does not select diffusion, M1 or VEF. Use a static medium, constant total extinction sigma_t and isotropic scattering sigma_s, and a positive isotropic source q. With angular measure dOmega/(4pi) and c=1, E, H and K are normalized energy, flux and pressure moments. Restore the common 4pi factor for unnormalized angular integrals. They do not validate inflow boundary factors, vacuum boundaries, absorber shadows, crossing beams, gas coupling, time evolution, multiple frequencies or relativistic transport. Selected passages of the original papers support the equations, closure and iteration. These examples do not reproduce Athena or all paper experiments, establish universal convergence or speedups, or certify fixed-grid asymptotic preservation in the diffusion limit. How to check the results Check positive intensity and E, tensor trace and eigenvalues, and face-flux balance first. Then inspect the linear residual and outer iteration, and compare fields, source-mode amplitudes and phases with the analytic reference. Keep spatial and angular rows separate, retaining the mesh-dependent HO/LO gap. Constant solutions, cross-derivative signs, omitted scattering feedback and a fixed one-third closure provide controls, so a small residual alone does not pass. Variable Eddington factor: a periodic 1D scattering-source control Computation for a fixed target Iteratively couple formal angular transport to independent moment equations and compare the spatially varying factor f with a closed-form reference. Position x and angular cosine mu are not two spatial dimensions. This periodic homogeneous educational control does not validate inflow boundaries, time evolution, material/fluid coupling, nonlinear FLD, general AP properties or speedup.
